subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Photosynthesis is described as endothermic because it...
options: transfers energy from the environment (light) into the plant
questions.explain: Photosynthesis takes in light energy, so it is an endothermic reaction.

questions.q: Which of these is a limiting factor for photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature can all limit the rate of photosynthesis.

questions.q: Why does the rate of photosynthesis eventually level off as light intensity keeps increasing?
options: Another factor such as CO2 or temperature becomes limiting
questions.explain: At high light, another factor (CO2 or temperature) limits the rate, so it plateaus.

questions.q: At low light intensity, what is most likely limiting photosynthesis?
questions.explain: When light is in short supply it limits the rate, so increasing light increases photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which pigment absorbs light energy for photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Chlorophyll in the chloroplasts absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.

questions.q: How is glucose made in photosynthesis used by the plant?
options: Used in respiration, converted to starch for storage, and to make cellulose
questions.explain: Glucose is used in respiration, stored as starch, and used to make cellulose, proteins and oils.

questions.q: What is the gas produced by photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Oxygen is released as a product of photosynthesis.

questions.q: How are leaves adapted for efficient photosynthesis?
options: Broad and thin with stomata and many chloroplasts
Thick and narrow with no stomata
questions.explain: Leaves are broad and thin with a large surface area, stomata for gas exchange and many chloroplasts.

questions.q: Why do palisade cells near the top of a leaf contain many chloroplasts?
options: To absorb maximum light for photosynthesis
questions.explain: Palisade mesophyll cells are packed with chloroplasts to capture as much light as possible.

questions.q: Which raw materials does a plant need for photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Photosynthesis requires carbon dioxide and water, plus light energy.

questions.q: In the starch test, which colour shows that starch is present?
questions.explain: Iodine solution turns blue-black where starch is present in the leaf.

questions.q: Why is a plant often kept in the dark before testing a leaf for starch?
options: To destarch the leaf so any new starch comes from the experiment
questions.explain: Destarching ensures any starch found afterwards was made during the test conditions.
